case_title: Javed Masood and Anr. v. State of Rajasthan
high_court_outcome: Set aside conviction under Sections 148 and 201; upheld conviction under Section 302 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that on the fateful day, accused persons equipped with deadly weapons reached the spot of occurrence and started inflicting injuries on the deceased and others. Thereafter, the accused persons fled away. The police van reached the spot and removed the deceased to the hospital where he was declared dead. A Parcha Bayan was lodged by a witness who was the brother of the deceased. The prosecution examined 33 witnesses and presented evidence of injuries found on the deceased's body. The trial court accepted the prosecution case and convicted the accused under Sections 148, 201, and 302 of the IPC. The High Court set aside the conviction under Sections 148 and 201 but upheld the conviction under Section 302. The Supreme Court, however, found that the evidence of the brother of the deceased, who was a highly interested witness, was not reliable. The evidence of an independent witness, a police constable, and others contradicted the presence of the brother of the deceased at the scene of the offense, leading to the conclusion that the prosecution's case was based on unreliable evidence.
